record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: Stable marriage; maximum number of stable matchings
record.original_question: For the Stable Marriage problem, determine the maximum number x_n of stable matchings that any instance of size n can admit, and in particular close the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds for x_n.

evidence.quote: This open problem, first posed by Gusfield and Irving [45], concerns finding the maximum number x_n of stable matchings admitted by any sm instance of size n.
Nevertheless, clearly there remains a large gap between the best known lower and upper bounds for x_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Stable Marriage problem, an instance of size n consists of a set of n men and a set of n women, where each person provides a strict total order (a preference list) over the members of the opposite sex. A matching is a bijection between the men and the women. Given a matching M, a pair (m, w) consisting of a man m and a woman w is called a blocking pair for M if m and w are not matched to each other in M, m strictly prefers w to his partner in M, and w strictly prefers m to her partner in M. A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Let x_n denote the maximum, over all Stable Marriage instances of size n, of the number of stable matchings admitted by the instance.

Problem: Determine the asymptotic behavior of x_n. In particular, close the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds, i.e., determine the exponential growth rate (and ideally the exact value) of x_n as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. The best known lower bound is approximately 2.28^n (Thurber, Irving–Leather constructions), while Karlin, Oveis Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018) proved a simply exponential upper bound c^n for some universal constant c, replacing the previous 2^{n log n - O(n)} bound. A substantial gap between these constants remains, and the exact asymptotic growth rate of x_n is still unknown.

status_evidence.title: A Simply Exponential Upper Bound on the Maximum Number of Stable Matchings
status_evidence.snippet: We show that f(n) ≤ c^n for some universal constant c, matching previous lower bounds up to the base of the exponent.
status_evidence.claim: The upper bound was improved to simply exponential, but a gap with the lower bound (~2.28^n) remains.

status_evidence.title: Pairing Things Off: Counting Stable Matchings (PhD thesis, Weber)
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bound on the maximum number of stable matchings remains around 2.28^n; the exact growth rate is still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The gap between lower and upper bounds for x_n persists.
